article_title: GLIMPSES OF A LONDON HOSPITAL: WESTMINSTER HOSPITAL
brief_extract: Perhaps the bravest testimony of all is the small war emergency kitchen which, formerly equipped for the children's wards only, houses on the second floor the cooking operations for all patients now in the hospital. In charge is Miss Ada Kibble, whose record is a proud one, as she cooked for a London hospital throughout the last war, and is proving her worth again in this one. Electricity, gas and steam are all used, but although each form has its merits, the Hospital pays tribute to the special reliability of electricity for cook- ing and lighting in time of war.

brief_extract: Everywhere one goes today in B.B.C. studios one sees girls in command; as home announcers like Prudence Neill, or Wendy Weddell in London; Constance Higginson in Ireland or Pamela Paterson in Scotland; as announcers for the Overseas Service, where Marjorie Anderson, Georgie Henschel and Beryl Measor write their own scripts daily and broadcast to the ends of the earth; as studio managers for the European broadcasts, or supervisors for the Monitoring Service. All these and many more, while not actually coming under the heading of "engineers," yet must necessarily know a good deal about the mechanisms which they control.
